lead: At a mark, rule 18 adds a second entitlement to right of way: mark-room. Who owes it is settled at the edge of the zone, whoever has right of way.

blocks.p: Rule 18 applies between boats that must leave a mark **on the same side** once **one of them is in the zone**: within three hull lengths of the boat nearer the mark. Hulls count, bowsprits do not. Until then only the right-of-way rules apply, whatever anyone hails.

fig.note: One bow in the zone: rule 18 now applies to both

blocks.p: A **mark** is anything the sailing instructions tell you to leave on a stated side: a buoy, an offset mark, a committee vessel. Other classes are included; a boat for whom it is not a mark of her leg is not. Each gate mark has its own zone.

blocks.p: A finishing mark is no exception: the outside boat gives mark-room there. And a mark you both leave on the same side is never a rule 19 obstruction.

sections.title: Settled when the first boat reaches the zone
refs: RRS definition Clear Astern and Clear Ahead; Overlap, RRS 18.2(a)(1)
RRS 18.2(a)(1), RRS 10, RRS definition Clear Astern and Clear Ahead; Overlap
RRS 18.2(a)(2), RRS definition Clear Astern and Clear Ahead; Overlap

blocks.p: Look at the boats when the first of them reaches the zone. If they are **overlapped**, the outside boat must from then on give the inside boat mark-room. If **not overlapped**, the first boat to reach the zone gets mark-room, even from a boat clear ahead of her.

The duty stays even if the overlap is later broken or a new one begins: an overlap gained inside the zone is too late. Right of way, size and hails change nothing: rule 18 needs no hail. Opposite-tack boats count as overlapped whenever rule 18 applies between them, as on a run. The outside boat gives room to every boat overlapped inside her.

If there is **reasonable doubt** that an overlap was obtained or broken in time, presume it was not. And no room is owed for an inside overlap gained from clear astern, or by tacking to windward, if the outside boat has been unable to give it ever since it began.

sections.title: Room to round, not room to win
refs: RRS definition Mark-Room, RRS definition Fetching

blocks.p: **Mark-room** is room to sail to the mark when your proper course is to sail close to it, then to round or pass it on the required side until it is left astern, a gybe at a gybe mark included. **Room** is the space needed in the existing conditions, current included, to manoeuvre promptly in a seamanlike way without touching the mark.

fig.note: Inside but windward: the wide loop is not mark-room

blocks.p: Inside but keeping clear, mark-room is all you have: swing wide for a tactical rounding and you must keep clear again. Inside with right of way, round as you like, giving room to keep clear when you change course (rule 16.1). The old clause on room to tack was removed in 2025.

sections.title: Coming in on port at a windward mark

blocks.p: At a mark left to port, rule 18.3 covers a boat that passes head to wind in the zone and is then on the same tack as a boat **fetching the mark**. Rule 18.2 is off between them, even if the other boat tacked in the zone too. The boat that tacked must not make the other sail above close-hauled to avoid contact, and gives her mark-room if she becomes overlapped inside.

fig.note: A tacks under your bow: she must not make you luff

blocks.p: Tacking in the zone is not forbidden: tack clear ahead and nobody is troubled. While still turning you keep clear under rule 13. Passing head to wind before the zone, or at a mark left to starboard, is outside 18.3.

sections.title: No sailing on past a leeward mark

blocks.p: Rule 18.4 limits a boat that is overlapped inside, has right of way and must gybe at the mark to sail her proper course. Until she gybes she sails no farther from the mark than that course needs; in 25 knots a later, safer gybe may be it. An inside boat that keeps clear or need not gybe is not bound, and the rule is off at a gate mark.

fig.note: On starboard, inside: the dashed course goes too far

blocks.p: Rule 18 ends between two boats once mark-room has been given: the leeward boat may luff again, and nothing is owed back. The entitlement also ends if the entitled boat passes head to wind or leaves the zone; if they are then overlapped at the mark, the outside one gives room.

blocks.rule: Mark-room is not right of way: the right-of-way boat often owes it.
